root.long_help:
owl is an intelligent Linux distributed operations tool, supporting:

	- Node management: node registry, groups, label management
	- Batch command execution: select targets by node, group, or label
	- Script transfer & execution: batch transfer and run shell scripts
	- Playbook execution: Ansible-like YAML playbook flow
	- File transfer: with P2P dissemination mode
	- AI assistant: perform ops via natural language

node.cmd.long:
Node management commands, supporting:

- list: List nodes
- add: Add a node
- update: Update a node
- remove: Remove a node
- import: Import nodes from a file
- export: Export nodes to a file
- status: View node status
- groups: Manage node groups
- labels: Manage node labels
- sample: Generate a sample node config file
node.list.long:
List all registered nodes, filterable by group, label, and status.

Available fields:
  id, name, address, port, user, status, groups, labels, last_check

Examples:
  owl node list                           # list all nodes
  owl node list --groups web              # list nodes in web group
  owl node list --label env=prod          # list nodes with env=prod
  owl node list --status online           # list online nodes
  owl node list -o json                   # JSON output
  owl node list --header id,address       # show only id and address columns
  owl node list --header id,name,labels:60  # 3 columns, labels width 60
  owl node list --header *                # show the default 8 fields
  owl node list --header *,id              # default fields + id last
  owl node list --header labels:60,*        # labels first, then other default fields
node.list.flag_status: Filter by status: online, offline, unknown
node.list.flag_header: Custom display fields and widths (format: id,address,labels:60,*,id)
node.add.long:
Add a new node to the management list.

Examples:
  # Basic usage
  owl node add node1 --name web-server-1 --address 192.168.1.10

  # With port and user
  owl node add node2 --name db-server-1 --address 192.168.1.20 --port 22 --user admin

  # With groups and multiple labels
  owl node add node3 --name app-server --address 192.168.1.30 --groups web,production --labels env=prod,appname=owl,region=us-east

  # Using SSH key auth
  owl node add node4 --name remote-server --address 192.168.1.40 --ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_rsa --labels env=staging,tier=backend
node.update.long:
Update existing node info, supporting partial field updates.

Examples:
  # Update node name
  owl node update node1 --name new-name

  # Update auth info
  owl node update node1 --password "new-password"

  # Update connection info
  owl node update node1 --address 10.0.0.1 --port 2222

  # Update groups and multiple labels
  owl node update node1 --groups web,prod --labels env=prod,appname=owl,tier=backend

  # Update status
  owl node update node1 --status online

node.check.short: Check node SSH connectivity (real SSH auth)
node.check.long:
Check node connectivity via a real SSH handshake, supporting key and password auth.
Tries key auth first, falls back to password auth.

You can filter nodes by group and label, or only check nodes that failed the last connection.

Note: unlike "owl node ping" (which only checks if the TCP port is open), check completes a full SSH authentication flow.
node.check.example:
# Check a single node
  owl node check node1

  # Check multiple nodes
  owl node check node1 node2 node3

  # Check all nodes
  owl node check --all

  # Only check nodes in the web group
  owl node check --groups web

  # Only check nodes with env=prod label
  owl node check --label env=prod

  # Only check nodes that failed last connection
  owl node check --failed

  # Combined filter: web group + prod env + only failed
  owl node check --groups web --label env=prod --failed

  # Adjust workers and timeout
  owl node check --all --workers 10 --timeout 30s

exec.cmd.long:
Command and script execution, supporting:

- run: Execute shell commands
- script: Execute script files

Note: use "owl playbook" for playbook execution
exec.run.long:
Execute a shell command on specified nodes with automatic connection management.

Examples:
  owl exec run uptime --nodes node1,node2
  owl exec run "df -h" --groups web
  owl exec run "systemctl status nginx" --label env=prod
  owl exec run uptime --status online
  owl exec run "sleep 30" --timeout 10s
  owl exec run "uptime" --format json
  owl exec run "df -h" --format detail
  owl exec run "sleep 5" --connect-timeout 5s --command-timeout 30s
  owl exec run "curl api.example.com" --retry 3 --retry-interval 2s
  owl exec run "long-running-script.sh" --async
  owl exec run "uptime" --nodes node1 --debug
  owl exec run "uptime" --nodes node1 --serial  # serial execution

exec.script.long:
Transfer and execute a script on the specified nodes.

Supports local script files and remote scripts by URL.

Execution methods:
  Default: upload to a remote file and execute (easier to debug and audit)
  --inline: send the content directly for execution (leaves no trace)

Examples:
  owl exec script deploy.sh --nodes web-01,web-02
  owl exec script ./scripts/install.sh --groups web --dest /tmp
  owl exec script backup.sh --args "--env prod" --label env=prod
  owl exec script init.sh --inline --nodes test-01  # execute content directly
  owl exec script setup.sh --keep --nodes all  # keep the script after execution
  owl exec script deploy.sh --timeout 10m

exec.script.flag_args: Arguments to pass to the script

file.cmd.long:
File transfer commands. Supports the following operations:

- upload: upload a file to nodes
- download: download a file from nodes
- transfer: node-to-node diffusion transfer (P2P mode)
file.common.err_list_nodes: Error: failed to get node list: %v
file.common.flag_groups: Select nodes by group (comma-separated, or repeat -g)
file.common.warn_history_db: Warning: failed to initialize history database: %v
file.download.cmd.long:
Download a file from remote nodes to local, with resume support.

Resume support:
- Automatically detects whether the remote node supports rsync
- Uses rsync if supported (resume)
- Falls back to scp otherwise

Examples:
  owl file download /var/log/app.log --nodes node1 --dest ./logs/
  owl file download /tmp/data.json --groups web --dest ./data/
  owl file download /var/log/app.log --nodes node1,node2 --dest ./logs/ --subdir
  owl file download /var/log/app.log --nodes node1,node2 --dest ./logs/ --name-format "{node}-{file}"
file.download.flag_parallel: Download from multiple nodes in parallel
file.transfer.cmd.long:
Diffuse a file from source nodes to other nodes using the self-diffusion transfer scheme.

The first N nodes are selected as sources, then the file is further transferred to the remaining nodes.

Examples:
  owl file transfer app.tar.gz --nodes node1,node2,node3,node4,node5 \
    --dest /opt/app/ --source-count 2
  owl file transfer data.zip --all-nodes --dest /data/ --fan-out 3
  owl file transfer db.tar.gz --groups database --source-count 1

ai.cmd.long:
Start the AI assistant interactive mode and perform distributed ops operations using natural language.

Supported features:
- Query node information: query node status, groups, and labels
- Run batch commands: execute commands on specified nodes
- Generate playbooks: generate Ansible-like YAML playbooks based on your requirements
- File transfer: transfer files to specified nodes

Examples:
  owl ai
  owl ai --model gpt-4o
  owl ai --provider dashscope --api-key sk-xxx
  echo "query all online nodes" | owl ai
